correctness.rationale: The exact domain is GP(10,3) and properly labelled three-edge-colourings; a single edge represents one whole bichromatic cycle swap. The backtracking proof systematically explores every legal colouring; a different exhaustive proof enumerates the sixty perfect matchings of the Petersen double cover and the alternations of their complementary even cycles. These independent constructions yield the same 192 colourings, 504 edges, component sizes, all-vertex distances, independent short-cycle counts and explicit odd-cycle and three-colour witnesses. Source files are part of this package and were executed successfully; no finite sampling is extrapolated to an infinite theorem. The 2021 class count tables use unlabelled colourings, and the sixfold palette multiplicity is respected.

originality.rationale: The same edge-Kempe move and class counts were studied previously, and the 2017 paper explicitly defines the entire edge-Kempe graph, so neither the framework nor generic triangle-freeness is claimed. The 2012 class-count paper, the complete relevant 2017 structural study, and the 2021 exhaustive class-count tables do not state the Desargues graph’s mixed bipartite/three-chromatic component decomposition or the per-component distance spheres and short-cycle counts. These statements do not follow from their displayed theorems or aggregate tables. All searched sources could miss an equivalent archived computation; this risk remains.
residual_risks: A computation equivalent to the seven complete component graphs could be present in unindexed code, older graph catalogues, or historical colouring-complex literature.

The 2021 census includes per-graph equivalence counts internally; a raw dataset might incidentally permit deriving the seven classes, though the published tables do not supply component metric or parity data.

value.rationale: The Desargues graph is a classical symmetric cubic bipartite double cover of the Petersen graph. Its exact optimal-edge-colouring reconfiguration dynamics separate into a 120-state bipartite sector and six 12-state three-chromatic sectors, with sharp diameters and uniform distance profiles. This is a substantive parity distinction in a standard local switching operation, and controls the period of nonlazy switching walks in each class. The specific component metric/odd-cycle classification answers motivated questions about edge-Kempe graph structure beyond counting equivalence classes; no general family theorem is claimed.
